clue.text: Circus float without a licence carries clown

indicators.note: carries means the shortened word holds the clown inside it
without tells us the letter a is left out of the word for licence

parts.note: abandon is licence in the sense of wild, unrestrained freedom
a wag is a joker or clown

explanation.surface: An unlicensed circus parade vehicle has a clown riding on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'licence' here is the noun for wild freedom, not a permit; 'without' drops the A from that synonym, and 'carries' puts the joker inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon was originally the decorated wagon carrying the band at the head of a circus parade.

clue.text: Vote against — there are seven for putting it in

definitions.meaning: to exclude a candidate from a club by a secret negative vote

definitions.text: there are seven for putting it in
definitions.meaning: in snooker the most valuable coloured ball scores seven points when potted

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a motion while seven members want it included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting it in' is snooker's potting: the black is the seven-point ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Members once voted secretly with white and black balls, a black one rejecting a candidate; in snooker the black ball scores seven.

clue.text: No man is this famous

parts.note: taken as written
Ted is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A claim that no ordinary man could ever be this well known.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone noted is well known and celebrated, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Dished, i.e., did the dishes

definitions.meaning: informally, dished means ruined or finished
cleaned the plates and pans after a meal

explanation.surface: Someone explains a pun on dishes and washing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished' in British slang means done for or ruined; the second sense is the British phrase for washing the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a failed person is finished, and washing plates after dinner is the everyday kitchen chore.

clue.text: Criminal causing anxiety in Germany

indicators.note: in places the word for anxiety within the abbreviation for Germany

parts.note: angst is a German-derived word for dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: Some criminal activity is spreading fear across Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised gang of violent criminals.

clue.text: Garment close to your upper parts

parts.note: nigh means near or close

indicators.note: the upper parts of the words to and your are their first letters

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing that fits snugly over the top of your body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' reads as an adjective on the garment but is NIGH; 'upper parts' takes the tops (first letters) of 'to your', giving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nighty is a nightdress, a loose garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Penny takes notes of debts, that's good

parts.note: IOUs are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Someone named Penny accepts written promises of debt and calls it virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Pious means devout and virtuous, which is a sense of good.

clue.text: Father sticks nose into Times leader

parts.note: someone who pries sticks their nose into other people's business

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of the word Times

explanation.surface: A dad meddles in the editorial page of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times leader' suggests the newspaper's editorial, but it is just the T that leads Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the title used for a Catholic clergyman.

clue.text: Those people in 25 are improving

indicators.note: in puts the word for those people inside the phrase for 25

parts.note: 25 down means standing upright, which is on end
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: People in some upright state are getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 25 down, ERECT, which here becomes ON END, holding THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting better after illness or difficulty, a recovering state.

clue.text: Arab leader of unstable movement, some say

indicators.note: some say signals that the word for the unsteady motion is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a shake is a trembling, unstable movement

explanation.surface: A ruler heading a shaky political movement, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' points to pronunciation: many speakers say this title like 'shake'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheik is the chief or head of an Arab tribe or family.

clue.text: One who works fan, but not quietly

indicators.note: but not tells us the letter for quietly is left out

parts.note: a partisan is a committed supporter or fan
P stands for piano, the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A labourer operates a fan, though not silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works fan' looks like operating a fan, but 'fan' is PARTISAN, from which 'but not' drops P.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker or craftsman.

clue.text: Cartilage in right leg — it's torn

indicators.note: torn means ripped apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A knee injury: cartilage in the right leg has been torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' scrambles R, LEG and ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough connective tissue in meat, essentially cartilage.

clue.text: Anchor gets linked, generally amidships

indicators.note: amidships means in the middle of the vessel, so the letters sit in the middle of these words

explanation.surface: A ship's anchor is chained up, usually at the middle of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidships' fits the nautical surface but signals letters hidden across 'linKED GEnerally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedge is a small anchor used to move a ship by hauling on its line.

clue.text: Poet's developed into a lush, if one may use the expression

definitions.text: if one may use the expression

indicators.note: into tells us the rearranged word goes inside the word for a drunkard

parts.note: a soak, like a lush, is a heavy drinker

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer has turned into a drunkard, so to put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lush' is a noun for a drunkard, not lavish; 'developed' rearranges the poet's letters and 'into' sets them inside the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase used to excuse a figurative or unusual way of speaking.

clue.text: When a murder is involved, nothing is hidden or protected

indicators.note: is hidden places the letter for nothing inside the rearranged letters
involved means tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Where a killing is concerned, nothing is kept secret or shielded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A MURDER; 'is hidden' places O within.
explanation.definitionFit: Armoured means covered with protective plating, like a tank.

clue.text: Dwarf in the militia?

parts.note: a tiny soldier read as a very small person, while the real sense is a citizen militiaman ready to fight at a minute's notice

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a very small person serving as a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: American Revolutionary militiamen were so named because they were ready to fight at a minute's notice; read with 'minute' as tiny, one becomes a dwarf.
explanation.definitionFit: These American colonial militiamen pledged to be ready at short notice, and minute also means tiny.

clue.text: 24 head off for an island

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word is cut away

parts.note: 24 refers to the answer at 24 across, a unit of heat

explanation.surface: A heading off to an island, though the number makes it cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is one of the Channel Islands, between Guernsey and Sark.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel Island near Guernsey, an example of an island.

clue.text: Meant more changes in a pressure gauge

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a measuring dial shows changes that mean more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges MEANT MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manometer is an instrument for measuring the pressure of gases or liquids.

clue.text: We have an agent out east, from there

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals that the letter for east is removed

parts.note: a steward is an agent who manages property for another

explanation.surface: We have a representative stationed out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out east' looks like a location but takes E out of STEWARD. 'from there' refers back to east: moving from the east means heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling away from the east is moving towards the west.

clue.text: To start right, I will have a pancake…

parts.note: taken as written
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: A cook begins well and will have a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' just says TO comes first; the ellipsis links this clue to the next two in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican bread made from maize, a kind of pancake.

clue.text: Calling for glib talk

definitions.meaning: a calling is a trade or occupation
smooth persuasive patter, as in a chat-up spiel someone shoots

explanation.surface: A vocation that consists of slick chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A line can mean an occupation and also a rehearsed piece of smooth talk.

clue.text: Obliged to see two points

parts.note: behold means to see or look at
E and N are two points of the compass, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone is required to look at a couple of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholden means indebted or under an obligation to someone.

clue.text: … to finish, I have a vegetable…

parts.note: the end is the finish
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: At the end of the meal someone has a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses make 18, 21 and 22 down read as one running sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad plant related to chicory, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: … because I do without

parts.note: for can mean because, as in for it was late
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: The speaker explains why they go without.
explanation.walkthrough: EGO is Latin for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to go without or abstain from something; this spelling is a recognised variant.

clue.text: Start off as a pedestrian group

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people
a pedestrian travels on foot

explanation.surface: A party of walkers begins their journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something on foot is to launch or initiate it.

clue.text: Stern cut short in part

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: severe means stern or strict

explanation.surface: A ship's rear section has been partially shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like a ship's rear but is an adjective, SEVERE, docked by 'cut short'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to divide or separate, a sense of part as a verb.

clue.text: The marines generate heat

parts.note: taken as written
RM stands for the Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry

explanation.surface: The armed forces produce warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat energy used for measuring gas supply.

clue.text: Standing before getting caught

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A batsman stood his ground before being caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, as when standing on one's feet.

clue.text: Siren, I note, is a mythical creature

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a siren
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A temptress is described as a legendary beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is a legendary undead being that drinks blood.

clue.text: It involves many people after a complaint

indicators.note: after signals that the container comes after the letter a
involves means the word it surrounds the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword many
men are people

explanation.surface: Lots of people get dragged into a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives L, fifty in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, and a complaint is a mild medical disorder.

clue.text: Order a cooker

definitions.meaning: to arrange or set out in a row

explanation.surface: A request to buy a kitchen stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To range things is to arrange them in order, and a kitchen range is a stove with ovens.

clue.text: Art seldom abused by an artist

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Artwork is rarely mistreated by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges ART SELDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An old master is a great European painter from before about 1800, or one of his works.
